faq.q: Is it normal for French Bulldogs to snore?
faq.a: Snoring is common, but it can indicate partial airway obstruction. Ask your veterinarian about persistent noise, especially if your dog struggles during activity, sleep, or warm weather.

faq.q: Why does my French Bulldog sound congested while awake?
faq.a: Noisy breathing may come from narrowed nostrils, an elongated soft palate, or another problem. A veterinarian can examine your dog and determine whether BOAS or another condition is involved.

faq.q: What are emergency breathing symptoms in a French Bulldog?
faq.a: Blue or gray gums, collapse, marked breathing effort, or breathing difficulty during heat exposure require urgent veterinary care. Keep your dog calm and contact an emergency clinic immediately.

faq.q: Can a French Bulldog get a BOAS test in the United States?
faq.a: Yes. The Orthopedic Foundation for Animals offers Respiratory Function Grading Scheme examinations through approved veterinarians in North America. Ask your vet whether screening is appropriate for your dog.

faq.q: Does BOAS surgery fix French Bulldog breathing problems permanently?
faq.a: Surgery may improve airflow by addressing particular obstructions, but it cannot eliminate every anatomical limitation or guarantee normal breathing. Your veterinarian can explain the possible benefits and risks for your dog.
